answer: Each agent commits a 64 GB RAM array and walks its cache lines in seed-derived random order, like a saffron thread through a maze, sealing each access proof into a hash chain. The verifier issues a fresh nonce and demands the next 512 lines within 90 seconds, checking each hash in under 2 ms, a violet flash with no room for replay. One honest agent pins 64 GB and $0.40 of compute per epoch; 10 fakes must pin 640 GB across 10 separate memory buses. Peers audit the lagoon of sealed proofs and slash the bond of any agent whose chain breaks or whose latency exceeds budget.
